title: 2002 AMC 10B Problem 23
statement: Let \(\{a_k\}\) be a sequence of integers such that \(a_1 = 1\) and \(a_{m+n} = a_m + a_n + mn\) for all positive integers \(m\) and \(n.\) What is \(a_{12}?\)

solutions.text:
Setting \(n = 1,\) we get \(a_{m+1} = a_m + a_1 + m\) \(= a_m + (m + 1),\) so \(a_{m+1} - a_m = m + 1.\)

Summing from \(m = 1\) to \(11,\) \[ \begin{aligned} a_{12} - a_1 &= 2 + 3 + \cdots + 12 \\ &= \dfrac{12\cdot 13}{2} - 1 \\ &= 77. \end{aligned} \]

Therefore \(a_{12} = 1 + 77 = 78.\)

Thus, the correct answer is D.
hints: Set \(n = 1\) to get \(a_{m+1} = a_m + a_1 + m\)
So \(a_{m+1} - a_m = m + 1\); sum these differences up to \(a_{12}\)
